record.paper_title: Known results and open problems in hypercomplex convexity
record.original_question: Let C be a convex Jordan curve in the plane R^2 with the property that whenever three vertices of a rectangle abcd lie on C, the fourth vertex also lies on C. Must C be a circle?

evidence.quote:
Mizel problem (Characterization of a circle). Let C be a convex Jordan
curve on a plane R2 with the following property:
For every rectangle abcd, if any three vertices are on C, then the fourth
vertex will be also on C. Is it true that C is a circle?
This problem was solved by Besicovitch and Danzer independently [16, 17].

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a convex Jordan curve (the boundary of a bounded convex region, homeomorphic to a circle). Assume $C$ has the following property: for every rectangle $abcd$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, if three of the four vertices $a,b,c,d$ lie on $C$, then the fourth vertex also lies on $C$. Prove or disprove: $C$ must be a circle.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the classical Mizel problem (the "rectangle property" characterization of the circle). It was solved affirmatively, independently by A. S. Besicovitch and L. Danzer in the 1950s–60s: a convex Jordan curve with the stated rectangle property must indeed be a circle.

status_evidence.title: Besicovitch, A characterization of the circular form of convex sets
status_evidence.snippet: Besicovitch proved that a convex curve having Mizel's rectangle property is a circle.
status_evidence.claim: The Mizel problem was solved affirmatively by Besicovitch.

status_evidence.title: Danzer, A characterization of the circle
status_evidence.snippet: Danzer independently gave a proof characterizing the circle by Mizel's rectangle property (Proc. Sympos. Pure Math., Convexity, 1963).
status_evidence.claim: Danzer independently solved the Mizel problem.
